To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel approach to automatic estimation of the innervation zones of the external anal and urethral sphincter from surface electromyography (sEMG) has been proposed and tested using simulations and a model of the generation of sEMG from the sphincters.
the proposed method is able to detect two IZs, and to estimate the IZ distribution in the EAS, and that this is possible even in the case of MUAP amplitude variation and MU distribution.

a novel method for localisation of the innervation zones (IZs) of the external sphincter has been developed and tested using a simulation model; the method can identify two IZs and estimate asymmetry of the EAS IZs; and the method is affected by surface motor unit amplitude, mucosa thickness and MU distribution, and can be used to prevent and investigate faecal incontinency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and testing of methods for the automatic analysis of EMG signals recorded from the external anal sphinctor.
the development and testing of an automatic method for the estimation of IZ distribution from surface EMG.
the development and testing of methods to estimate the location of IZs of the EAS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach is a useful tool for the analysis of surface EMG signals from EAS.
the proposed method can provide an estimate of IZ distribution and can be useful for the diagnosis and investigation.
the method is promising for the estimation of IZs of the EAS, and that further studies are needed to validate it in clinical settings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed method can be used to estimate the IZ location of EAS, and that it is robust with respect to the variability of the parameters used in the model.
we developed a method to estimate the innervation zone distribution of the external anal spinchter muscle from surface EMG.

the automatic method is able to detect the IZ location and to quantify the IZ distribution in the case of the external anal muscle, and this could be useful in the investigation and diagnosis of incontinence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the automatic localisation of the IZs is possible with the use of the proposed method and that it is able to estimate the IZ distribution with a good accuracy.
the method proposed is robust and able to estimate the IZ location even when the IZ is located in a different depth than the IZ of the other muscle.

the proposed method can be applied to real data, and it can be useful in the diagnosis of incontinence, in the investigation of the causes of incontinence and in the assessment of the effects of surgical interventions.
